summary: Completed full paired NodePool/NodeClass review; removed invented defaults and unsupported EC2NodeClass fields while preserving current supported T families, instance profiles, kernel tuning, KMS/CA and Pod-network customization.
findings: Purported AWS-managed default pool specs may be invented/outdated (architectures/capacity types/generation/size/disruption settings); verify current docs rather than apply these defaults.
System-pool CoreDNS/kube-proxy explanation conflicts with Auto Mode node system services.
Auto NodeClass borrows amiFamily, blockDeviceMappings, userData and metadataOptions from self-managed EC2NodeClass; needs actual AWS NodeClass schema.
Extended NodeClass uses top-level kmsKeyID and certificateBundles.content with fake PEM; wrong EBS/instance-store encryption claim and missing role/instance profile in second example.
Resource limits are vCPU/memory, not maximum node count; 4000Gi is not exactly4TB; weight is provisioning preference, not scheduler priority/security isolation.
Check actual current burstable-instance support for dev t-family; preserve supported customization via current fields rather than deleting valid recent features.
Current built-ins both use On-Demand C/M/R generation>=5; general-purposeAMD64, systemAMD64+ARM64. Replaced guessed default manifests with read-only inspection and documented removal/drain semantics.
Auto Mode IMDSv2/hop1 are fixed; hostNetwork is a distinct exposure case. Corrected false AL2023/Bottlerocket choice and metadataOptions settings.
instanceProfile is valid (eks prefix, mutually exclusive with role); T-family burstables are currently supported above size/CPU minima. Retained these legitimate options.
Replaced blockDeviceMappings/userData with ephemeralStorage and supported advancedCompute.kernel.sysctl. KMS applies to root/data EBS, not arbitrary local-NVMe/PVC encryption.

CA bundles use base64 certificateBundles.data; real PEM validation, private-key rejection and account/region checking replace fake certificate content. Pod subnet/SG selectors paired, with per-NodeClass/SNAT/hostNetwork limitations.

Clarified aggregate resource quantities, no hard spending cap, provisioning weights, and selector+toleration placement rather than tenant-security guarantees. No numeric benchmark rerun or cloud execution.
